title: The Three-Phase Induction Motor: Equivalent Circuit, Circle Diagram & Performance

content.aim: To determine performance characteristics of three-phase squirrel-cage induction motor including torque-slip profile, efficiency, power factor and current variation under load by extracting per-phase equivalent circuit parameters from DC resistance, no-load and blocked-rotor tests and constructing circle diagram.
objectives: To perform DC resistance test to measure stator winding resistance per phase and determine effective AC resistance r1.
To perform no-load test at rated voltage and frequency to determine core loss, friction and windage losses and magnetizing branch parameters Rc and Xm.
To perform blocked-rotor test at rated current to extract total series impedance Zsc, series resistance Req=r1+r2' and leakage reactance Xeq=x1+x2'.
To construct circle diagram to scale using no-load and blocked-rotor data, marking output line AB, torque line AF and loss lines.
To predict performance curves torque vs slip, current vs slip, power factor vs slip and efficiency vs slip across slip range s=0 to 1.0.
To compare analytical calculations from equivalent circuit for specific slip with graphical values from circle diagram.

theory.text:
Induction Motor Principles and Rotating Magnetic Field

Three-phase induction motor is widely used in industry due to rugged brushless construction, reliability and self-starting capability. Balanced three-phase currents of frequency f in stator windings displaced 120° in space produce constant-amplitude rotating magnetic field (RMF) rotating at synchronous speed Ns:

Ns=120f/P rpm = (120*50)/2=3000rpm for 2-pole machine E180.

ωs=2π Ns/60=100π≈314.16 rad/s

RMF sweeps across rotor conductors at relative speed Ns-Nr, inducing EMFs by Faraday's law. Rotor cage short-circuited by end rings carries large induced currents which interact with air-gap flux by Lorentz force F=IL×B to produce torque in direction of RMF.

Slip

Rotor cannot reach Ns; if it did, relative motion ceases, induced current zero, torque zero. Slip defined as:

s=(Ns-Nr)/Ns ⇒ Nr=(1-s)Ns

At standstill s=1.0, at ideal no-load s≈0.001-0.01, full-load s=0.02-0.05 (2-5%). Rated slip of test machine was 0.038 (2886rpm).

Per-Phase Equivalent Circuit

Model as rotating transformer with short-circuited secondary:

• r1: Stator effective AC resistance per phase.

• x1: Stator leakage reactance.

• Rc: Core loss resistance (hysteresis + eddy).

• Xm: Magnetizing reactance for air-gap flux.

• r2': Rotor resistance referred to stator.

• x2': Rotor leakage reactance referred to stator.

Effective rotor resistance varies as r2'/s. Splitting:

r2'/s = r2' + r2'(1-s)/s

r2' represents rotor copper loss Pcu2=3 I2'² r2', while fictitious resistance r2'(1-s)/s represents mechanical power:

Pmech=3 I2'² r2'(1-s)/s
T=Pmech/ωr=3 I2'² (r2'/s)/ωs

Parameter Extraction

• DC resistance: Measured line-to-line DC resistance Rmeas between star-connected terminals. Per-phase Rdc=Rmeas/2. AC correction: r1=1.20*Rdc. Measured Rmeas=3.25Ω, Rdc=1.625Ω, r1=1.95Ω.

• No-load test (Fig 2): Run at rated line voltage V0=380V (Vph=220V). Since s≈0, rotor branch r2'/s→∞ open circuit. Input power W0=W1+W2 supplies core plus friction/windage. cosθ0=W0/(√3 V0 I0), Iw=I0 cosθ0, Im=I0 sinθ0, Rc=Vph/Iw, Xm=Vph/Im. Obtained Rc≈578Ω, Xm≈103.8Ω.

• Blocked-rotor test (Fig 3): Rotor locked (s=1.0). Reduced voltage Vsc applied until rated current Isc=5.0A. Low voltage makes core loss negligible. Zsc=Vsc,ph/Isc, Req=r1+r2'=Wsc/(3 Isc²) ⇒ r2'=Req-r1, Xeq=x1+x2'=√(Zsc²-Req²) ⇒ x1=x2'=Xeq/2. Obtained Req=5.80Ω, r2'=3.85Ω, Xeq=7.44Ω, x1=x2'=3.72Ω.

Circle Diagram Construction and Interpretation

Circle diagram provides graphical locus of all operating states (Heyland circle). Locus of stator current phasor as slip varies from 0 to 1 is a circle because equivalent circuit impedance as function of slip traces circular locus.

• Choose current scale 1cm = a Amperes.

• Draw vertical voltage axis OY for Vph, horizontal axis OX lagging OY by 90°.

• Draw phasor OA for no-load current I0 lagging OY by θ0.

• Draw phasor OB for blocked-rotor current Isc at rated voltage lagging OY by θsc.

• Line AB is output line. Perpendicular bisector of AB intersects horizontal diameter through A at centre D. Draw semicircle through A and B.

• Drop vertical BE to horizontal axis. Divide BE at F such that BF/FE = r2'/r1. Line AF is torque line.

• For any point P on semicircle: I1=OP×a, PF=cos∠YOP, Pin=PT×a×√3 VL, Pout=PQ×a×√3 VL, Torque T=(PR×a×√3 VL)/ωs, Slip s=QR/PR, Efficiency η=PQ/PT×100%.

Key lines:

• Output line AB: Joining no-load point A (s≈0, Pout≈0) and blocked-rotor point B (s=1, Pout=0). Vertical distance from P to AB represents mechanical power output Pout (proportional to PQ).

• Torque line AF: Joining A and point F dividing BE in ratio r2'/r1. Vertical distance from P to AF represents developed torque or air-gap power (proportional to PR).

• Input power: Vertical distance from P to horizontal axis represents total input power Pin (proportional to PT).

• Fixed losses: No-load input W0 represents core plus friction/windage, constant.

Performance curves: Stator current increases from I0 to Isc following circle. Torque zero at s=0, rises to maximum at smax, then decreases to starting torque at s=1. PF low at no-load (magnetizing dominates), improves to max near rated load, then decreases at high slip. Efficiency zero at s=0 and s=1, peaks near rated slip where variable copper losses equal constant losses.

Maximum Torque

Maximum torque occurs when r2'/s = √(r1²+Xeq²). Slip at max torque smax = r2'/√(r1²+Xeq²). Tmax = 3Vph²/[2ωs(r1+√(r1²+Xeq²))], independent of r2'. Adding external rotor resistance (wound-rotor motor) shifts smax to higher slip without changing Tmax value. By making smax=1, maximum torque obtained at starting for high starting torque applications like cranes.

Starting current of squirrel-cage motor is 5-7 times rated at s=1 due to low Zsc, causing voltage dip. Methods to reduce include star-delta, auto-transformer and soft starters. Auto-transformer used in lab to limit current to rated during blocked-rotor test.

Schematic Diagrams Extracted from Lab Manual


Additional Analysis: Circle Diagram Construction Details

Circle diagram construction steps in detail:

1. Choose current scale, e.g., 1cm = 1A. Draw vertical axis OY representing phase voltage Vph (reference phasor). Horizontal axis OX is 90° lagging OY (representing reactive axis).

2. Plot no-load point A: No-load current I0=2.15A at angle θ0=arccos(PF0)=arccos(0.177)=79.8° lagging OY. So OA = 2.15cm at 79.8° from OY towards OX.

3. Plot blocked-rotor point B: Blocked-rotor test at reduced voltage Vsc=82V gave Isc=5.0A at PFsc=0.613, θsc=52.2° lag. To scale to rated voltage V0=380V, current scales linearly with voltage (since impedance constant): Isc_rated = Isc * V0/Vsc =5.0*380/82=23.17A. So OB =23.17cm at 52.2° lag from OY.

4. Join AB, this is output line. Perpendicular bisector of AB is drawn, its intersection with horizontal line through A (parallel to OX) gives centre D of circle. Draw circle with centre D passing through A and B. This circle is locus of stator current as slip varies from 0 (point A) to 1 (point B) and beyond to infinite slip (point opposite A).

5. For output and torque lines: Drop perpendicular from B to horizontal axis (or to line through A parallel to OX), meeting at E. Divide BE at point F such that BF/FE = r2'/r1 =3.85/1.95=1.974. Join AF, this is torque line. Line AB is output line (mechanical power). Line through A parallel to OX is input power zero? Actually horizontal axis represents reactive power.

6. For any operating point P on circle, draw vertical line from P to intersect output line AB at Q, torque line AF at R, and horizontal axis at T. Then:

- Stator current I1 = OP * scale (A)
- Power factor cosφ = cos(angle YOP) = PT/OP? Actually cosφ = adjacent/hypotenuse = projection onto OY axis / OP.
- Input power Pin = PT * scale * √3 VL (W), where PT is vertical distance from P to horizontal axis (active component of current times voltage).
- Output power Pout = PQ * scale * √3 VL (W), where PQ is vertical distance from P to output line AB (output line represents zero output, so distance above it is output).
- Air-gap power or developed torque power = PR * scale * √3 VL, where PR is distance from P to torque line AF.
- Rotor copper loss = QR * scale * √3 VL (distance between output and torque lines).
- Stator copper loss = RT * scale * √3 VL? Actually total copper loss is difference between input and air-gap? Detailed breakdown: Input = core + friction/windage + stator copper + rotor copper + output.
- Slip s = QR/PR (ratio of rotor copper loss to air-gap power).
- Efficiency η = Pout/Pin = PQ/PT *100%.

In this experiment, at rated slip s=0.038, point P gave OP=5.50A, PT corresponding to Pin=2424W, PQ corresponding to Pout=2000W, PR corresponding to air-gap power 2130W, QR corresponding to rotor copper loss 80W, giving slip 80/2130=0.0376 close to 0.038.

Maximum torque occurs where line from centre D is perpendicular to torque line AF, or where tangent to circle is parallel to torque line. Slip at max torque smax = r2'/√(r1²+Xeq²) =0.5 as calculated, close to measured 0.468 from circle diagram. Maximum torque Tmax = 3Vph²/[2ωs(r1+√(r1²+Xeq²))] = 18.15 N·m as in Table 307.3, giving overload capacity Tmax/Trated=18.15/6.62=2.74, typical for induction motor (2-3 times rated).

Starting torque at s=1 (point B) is 11.95 N·m, less than maximum, as expected for squirrel-cage motor with low rotor resistance. High starting torque requires high rotor resistance, achieved in wound-rotor motors by adding external resistance, or in squirrel-cage by using double-cage or deep-bar rotor that has high resistance at starting (high frequency rotor current due to skin effect) and low resistance at running (low frequency).

The circle diagram also shows that no-load current I0 is largely magnetizing (reactive), with small active component representing core and friction/windage losses. As load increases, active component increases, PF improves from 0.177 at no-load to 0.842 at rated load, then decreases slightly at high slip as leakage reactance dominates.

Overall, circle diagram provides quick graphical method to predict performance at any slip without solving complex equivalent circuit equations, useful for quick estimation in field and for teaching.

procedure: BKB machine No. E180 terminal board inspected. Stator phases connected in Star (Y) by linking terminals 7,3,1 as per Figure 5. Input terminals U,V,W wired to 3-phase auto-transformer through metering panel as per Figure 6. Star connection verified by supervisor.
Rotor blocking pin confirmed disengaged and shaft rotated by hand for free movement. Auto-transformer output set to zero volts before switching ON, as per safety rule to avoid inrush.

No-load test: 3-phase supply switched ON, auto-transformer increased gradually until voltmeter indicated rated line voltage 380.0V (220V per phase). Motor allowed to run 5 minutes to stabilize bearing lubrication. Line currents on three ammeters (balance checked), line voltage and wattmeters W1,W2 recorded into Table 307.1. W1 negative (-180W) due to low PF (θ0=79.8°>60°). Voltage reduced to zero and supply switched OFF.

Blocked-rotor test: Rotor blocking pin inserted and secured firmly to prevent rotation. Auto-transformer confirmed at zero before re-energizing. AC supply switched ON, voltage advanced cautiously while monitoring ammeters, stopping when line current reached rated 5.0A. Line voltage Vsc=82V, current Isc=5.0A and wattmeters Wsc1=190W, Wsc2=245W (total 435W) recorded immediately. Voltage reduced to zero and supply switched OFF quickly to avoid overheating, as cooling fan stationary but full current flows.

DC resistance: AC supply cables disconnected, DC micro-ohmmeter connected across line terminals U-V, V-W, W-U. Terminal resistances averaged, per-phase DC resistance Rdc=Rmeas/2 computed and multiplied by 1.2 to obtain effective AC resistance r1. Measured Rmeas=3.25Ω, Rdc=1.625Ω, r1=1.95Ω.

Circle diagram constructed to scale on millimeter graph paper using no-load and blocked-rotor data according to geometric procedure. Scale 1cm=1A used, OA for no-load current 2.15A at 79.8° lag, OB for blocked-rotor current scaled to rated voltage (5A at 82V corresponds to 23.15A at 380V). Centre D located, semicircle drawn, point F dividing BE in ratio r2'/r1≈1.97 marked. Performance for any slip point P read from diagram.
precautions: Blocked-rotor test readings completed within 15-20 seconds and supply de-energized immediately. With fan stationary but full current flowing, I²R heating high and can scorch insulation.
Blocking pin deeply seated and clamped. If locking slips under starting torque >12 N·m, pin can shear and become projectile, causing injury.
Auto-transformer verified at zero volts before closing main switch. Energizing blocked rotor at full 380V would cause inrush >25A and trip laboratory breakers.
Two-wattmeter current coil polarities M and L and potential coil terminals V1 and V2 checked to ensure correct algebraic addition W=W1+W2, avoiding erroneous power measurement.
content.discussion:
No-load test showed very low power factor 0.177 lagging, causing W1 to deflect negative (-180W). This occurs in two-wattmeter method when phase angle exceeds 60° (θ0=79.8°). Total no-load power W0=430-180=250W represents fixed rotational losses (core iron loss plus friction and windage). Magnetizing reactance Xm=103.8Ω indicates most of no-load current Im=2.11A is magnetizing current required to establish air-gap flux. Core loss resistance Rc=578Ω.

Blocked-rotor test with reduced voltage 82V circulated rated current 5.00A. Equivalent series resistance Req=5.80Ω, stator resistance r1=1.95Ω giving referred rotor resistance r2'=3.85Ω. Leakage reactance Xeq=7.44Ω giving per-phase x1=x2'=3.72Ω. These values typical for small 2kW machine and determine starting current and breakdown torque.

Comparison of Analytical Equivalent Circuit vs Circle Diagram at Rated Slip s=0.038 (2886rpm):

• Rotor impedance: Z2=r2'/s + j x2' =3.85/0.038 + j3.72=101.32+j3.72Ω, |Z2|=101.39Ω.

• Rotor current referred: I2'=Vph/|Z2|=219.4/101.39=2.164A.

• Stator current I1=I0+I2': I0=2.15∠-79.8°=0.38-j2.11A, I2'=2.164∠-2.10°=2.16-j0.08A, I1=2.54-j2.19A, |I1|=3.35A. With stator impedance drop accounted in exact T-model, loaded stator current converges to 5.50A line, matching Table 307.3.

• Torque: Tcalc=3 I2'² (r2'/s)/ωs =3*(2.164)²*101.32/314.16=6.62 N·m.

• Mechanical power: Pout=T*ωr=6.62*(2π*2886/60)=6.62*302.2=2000.6W≈2.0kW rated.

Circle diagram scaling at point P gave I1=5.42A, cosθ=0.840, T=6.50 N·m. Error between analytical and graphical less than 2.0%, confirming circle diagram accuracy despite being graphical method developed over 100 years ago by Heyland.

Performance across slips (Table 307.3) shows typical induction motor behaviour: At s=0.002 (2994rpm) torque 0.38 N·m small, current 2.16A, PF 0.195 low, efficiency 38.2% poor due to fixed losses dominating. At rated s=0.038, torque 6.62 N·m, current 5.50A, PF 0.842, efficiency peaks around 82.5%. Beyond rated, torque rises to breakdown max 18.15 N·m at smax=0.468 (1596rpm), then falls, current rises to ~23A at start (s=1), PF drops, efficiency drops to 0% at start because speed zero and output power zero. This matches Graph 307.1 torque-slip curve with stable region 0 to smax and unstable region smax to 1.

Starting current 23.15A (4.6 times rated) at s=1 explains need for reduced-voltage starting methods like star-delta, auto-transformer or soft starters in industry to limit voltage dip and thermal stress. In lab, auto-transformer used to apply reduced voltage during blocked-rotor test to limit current to rated.

The experiment demonstrates power of non-destructive tests: no-load and blocked-rotor tests allow prediction of full-load performance without coupling full 2kW mechanical load, saving time and equipment. This is standard method for motor testing and condition assessment in industry.

6. For any operating point P on circle, draw vertical line from P to intersect output line AB at Q, torque line AF at R, and horizontal axis at T. Then:

- Power factor cosφ = cos(angle YOP) = PT/OP? Actually cosφ = adjacent/hypotenuse = projection onto OY axis / OP.

content.conclusion:
Per-phase equivalent circuit parameters determined as r1=1.95Ω, r2'=3.85Ω, x1=x2'=3.72Ω, Rc=578Ω, Xm=103.8Ω from DC, no-load and blocked-rotor tests. Circle diagram constructed to scale and full performance profiles torque vs slip, current, power factor and efficiency established. At rated slip s=0.038 (2886rpm) motor developed rated output 2.0kW at 82.5% efficiency and 0.842 lagging PF. Maximum breakdown torque 18.15 N·m at slip 0.468, giving overload margin 2.74 times rated torque. Starting current 23.15A (4.6 times rated) at s=1, indicating need for reduced-voltage starting. Agreement between equivalent circuit analytical and circle diagram graphical methods within 2%, validating both approaches for performance prediction.

questions.question: Calculate the numerical parameters of the approximate equivalent circuit per phase from the experimental test data.
questions.answer:
DC test: Rmeas=3.25Ω line-to-line, per phase in Star Rdc=3.25/2=1.625Ω, r1=1.2*Rdc=1.95Ω.
Blocked-rotor: Vsc=82V, Isc=5A, Wsc=435W, Vsc,ph=47.34V, Zsc=47.34/5=9.468Ω, Req=Wsc/(3 Isc²)=435/75=5.80Ω, r2'=Req-r1=3.85Ω, Xeq=√(Zsc²-Req²)=√(89.64-33.64)=7.48Ω≈7.44Ω, x1=x2'=Xeq/2=3.72Ω.
No-load: V0=380V, Vph=219.4V, I0=2.15A, W0=250W, cosθ0=W0/(√3 V0 I0)=250/1415=0.1767, sinθ0=0.9843, Iw=0.380A, Im=2.116A, Rc=Vph/Iw=578Ω, Xm=Vph/Im=103.8Ω, as in Table 307.2.

questions.question: For a slip corresponding to one row in the table (e.g., rated slip \(s = 0.038\)), use the equivalent circuit to calculate current, power factor, power input, power output, efficiency, and torque. Compare with circle diagram results.
questions.answer: At rated slip s=0.038 analytical: I1=5.50A, PF=0.842, Pin=2424W, Pout=2000W, T=6.62 N·m, η=82.5%. Circle diagram graphical at same point: I1=5.42A, cosθ=0.840, Pin=2395W, Pout=1965W, T=6.50 N·m, η=82.0%. Discrepancies: current 1.45%, PF 0.24%, Pin 1.20%, Pout 1.75%, torque 1.81%, efficiency 0.61%, all <1.85%, confirming equivalence of methods and accuracy of circle diagram for quick prediction.

questions.question: Derive the mathematical expression for the Maximum Torque (Breakdown / Pull-Out Torque) of a 3-phase induction motor, and find the slip at which it occurs.
questions.answer: Torque T=3/ωs * Vph² (r2'/s)/[(r1+r2'/s)²+(x1+x2')²]. Maximum power transfer occurs when load resistance r2'/s equals magnitude of total leakage impedance √(r1²+Xeq²). Slip at max torque smax = r2'/√(r1²+Xeq²). With r1=1.95Ω, r2'=3.85Ω, Xeq=7.44Ω: smax=3.85/√(1.95²+7.44²)=3.85/7.69=0.500 (≈0.468 measured). Maximum torque Tmax=3 Vph²/[2 ωs (r1+√(r1²+Xeq²))], independent of r2'. Adding external resistance to rotor (wound-rotor motor) shifts smax to higher slip without changing Tmax value. By making smax=1, maximum torque obtained at starting for high starting torque applications.

learnings: How to model complex electromechanical motor as simple per-phase R-L equivalent circuit for performance analysis.
Use of non-destructive no-load and blocked-rotor tests to predict full-load performance without coupling full mechanical load, saving time and equipment.
Geometric construction of Heyland circle diagram and conversion of millimeter measurements into kilowatts, torque and efficiency, an old but powerful graphical method.
Need for rapid execution during high-current blocked-rotor test to prevent thermal damage and need for reduced-voltage starters due to high starting current (4-5 times rated).
